Every exam item evaluates one or more of the four College Board Mathematical Practices:

PracticeTitleCore Competency & Observable Behaviors
MP 1Procedural & Symbolic FluencySolve equations symbolically, evaluate trigonometric and inverse trigonometric values exactly, rewrite algebraic expressions, and compose/invert functions without technology.
MP 2Multiple RepresentationsTranslate seamlessly between algebraic formulas, numerical data tables, coordinate graphs, and verbal rate-of-change descriptions.
MP 3Communication & ReasoningJustify conclusions with formal mathematical arguments, state theorems and verify their hypotheses (e.g. IVT, continuity), and express asymptotic end behaviors using limit notation.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (AP Precalculus Exam Format & Modeling Framework)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

A student has 80 minutes to complete the 28 non-calculator questions in Section I Part A. What is the average time available per question in minutes and seconds?

Divide total time by number of questions: \[ \frac{80\text{ minutes}}{28\text{ questions}} = \frac{20}{7} \approx 2.857\text{ minutes}. \] Convert the decimal fraction to seconds: \[ 0.857 \times 60 \approx 51.4\text{ seconds} \implies 2\text{ minutes and }51\text{ seconds per question}. \]

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — AP Precalculus Exam Format & Modeling Framework (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Consider the quadratic function \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \). What are the x-intercepts of the graph of this function?

Step-by-Step Solution: To find the x-intercepts of the graph of a function, we need to find the values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) = 0 \). For the given function \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \), we set \( x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0 \). This is a quadratic equation that can be solved by factoring. We look for two numbers that multiply to 3 and add to -4. These numbers are -1 and -3. Thus, we can factor the equation as \( (x - 1)(x - 3) = 0 \). Setting each factor to zero, we get \( x - 1 = 0 \) or \( x - 3 = 0 \). Solving these equations gives \( x = 1 \) and \( x = 3 \). Therefore, the x-intercepts are \( (1, 0) \) and \( (3, 0) \).

Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Pacing, Calculator Policy & Rate-of-Change Modeling Taxonomy

body.en: Determine function types from discrete data tables by analyzing consecutive differences and constant multiplicative ratios.

caption.en: AP Precalculus exam weighting across the three core assessed units: Unit 1 (35%), Unit 2 (35%), and Unit 3 (30%).

label.en: ● Analytical Model Selection Taxonomy: Finite Differences & Consecutive Quotients

body.en:
Given a discrete sequence of points \((x_k, y_k)\) with equal step size \(\Delta x = x_{k+1} - x_k = h\):

  • Linear Function \(f(x) = mx + b\): First differences are strictly constant: \[ \Delta y_k = y_{k+1} - y_k = m \cdot h = \text{constant}. \]
  • Quadratic Function \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\): First differences change linearly, and second differences are strictly constant: \[ \Delta^2 y_k = \Delta y_{k+1} - \Delta y_k = 2a \cdot h^2 = \text{constant}. \]
  • Polynomial of Degree \(n\): The \(n\)-th finite difference is strictly constant: \[ \Delta^n y_k = a_n \cdot n! \cdot h^n = \text{constant}. \]
  • Exponential Function \(f(x) = C \cdot b^x\): Consecutive output ratios are strictly constant: \[ \frac{y_{k+1}}{y_k} = \frac{C b^{x_k + h}}{C b^{x_k}} = b^h = \text{constant growth/decay factor}. \]

• Section I Part A (No Calculator — 28 Qs / 80 min): Focus on exact algebraic manipulation, unit circle values, factor theorem, and sign charts.
  • Section I Part B (Graphing Calculator — 12 Qs / 50 min): Over 4 minutes per question. Problems require numerical root solving, graphing intersections, and regression curve fitting.
  • Section II (4 FRQs / 60 min): Allot 15 minutes per free-response question. All 4 FRQs permit a graphing calculator. Round non-exact numerical answers to 3 decimal places unless specified otherwise.

A function \(f(x)\) has the table of values: \((1, 8), (2, 14), (3, 24), (4, 38)\). Determine whether a linear or quadratic model is appropriate by examining finite differences.

First differences \(\Delta y\): \[ 14 - 8 = 6, \quad 24 - 14 = 10, \quad 38 - 24 = 14. \] Because first differences are not constant, a linear model is not appropriate. Second differences \(\Delta^2 y\): \[ 10 - 6 = 4, \quad 14 - 10 = 4. \] Because the second differences are constant, a quadratic model is appropriate.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

A table of values for a positive function \(g(x)\) over equally spaced inputs \(x = 0, 1, 2, 3\) produces outputs \(g(0) = 4, g(1) = 12, g(2) = 36, g(3) = 108\). Which function family best models \(g(x)\), and what is the constant growth factor per unit increase in \(x\)?
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

A table of values for a positive function \(g(x)\) over equally spaced inputs \(x = 0, 1, 2, 3\) produces outputs \(g(0) = 4, g(1) = 12, g(2) = 36, g(3) = 108\). Which function family best models \(g(x)\), and what is the constant growth حلّل per unit increase in \(x\)?

solution.en: Calculate the consecutive ratios of consecutive outputs: \[ \frac{g(1)}{g(0)} = \frac{12}{4} = 3, \quad \frac{g(2)}{g(1)} = \frac{36}{12} = 3, \quad \frac{g(3)}{g(2)} = \frac{108}{36} = 3. \] Because the ratio of outputs is constant for equal-length input intervals, \(g(x)\) is an exponential function with a constant growth factor of 3.
solution.ar: احسب consecutive ratios of consecutive outputs: \[ \frac{g(1)}{g(0)} = \frac{12}{4} = 3, \quad \frac{g(2)}{g(1)} = \frac{36}{12} = 3, \quad \frac{g(3)}{g(2)} = \frac{108}{36} = 3. \] Because the ratio of outputs is constant for equal-length input intervals, \(g(x)\) is an exponential function with a constant growth حلّل of 3.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — FRQ Task Models, Justification Protocol & Scoring Rubrics

body.en: Master the four Free-Response Question task models, standard justification frameworks, and precise presentation guidelines required by College Board scorers.

label.en: ● The 4 AP Precalculus FRQ Task Models

body.en:
Section II contains four distinct 6-point task models (24 total points, 50% of composite score):

Task ModelFocus AreaCalculator PolicyKey Prompts & Expectations
FRQ 1Function ConceptsGraphing CalculatorCompute average rate of change (AROC) on \([a, b]\), estimate instantaneous trends, evaluate composite/inverse functions, and find extrema or domain/range restrictions.
FRQ 2Modeling Non-Periodic ContextGraphing CalculatorPerform regression analysis (linear, quadratic, exponential, or power), construct a piecewise or logistic model, interpret coefficients in context with units, and solve equations for threshold times.
FRQ 3Modeling Periodic ContextGraphing CalculatorConstruct a sinusoidal model \(f(t) = A\sin(B(t-C)) + D\) from amplitude, midline, and period data; identify extrema; and determine time intervals where outputs exceed a threshold.
FRQ 4Symbolic ManipulationsNo CalculatorSolve trigonometric equations exactly over \([0, 2\pi)\), prove trigonometric identities, simplify rational/logarithmic expressions, and manipulate vectors, matrices, or polar curves algebraically.

label.en: ▲ The 4 Core FRQ Commandments of AP Precalculus

body.en:
• 1. Always Use Function Notation & Units: When modeling real-world quantities, define variables with units (e.g., 'let \(t\) be time in hours since midnight'). Include units in your final answers.
  • 2. Justify Using Rates of Change (AROC): When asked whether a model is appropriate, explain using rates of change: linear functions have constant first differences, quadratic functions have constant second differences, and exponential functions have constant proportional growth ratios.
  • 3. Show Setup Before Calculator Results: Even with a graphing calculator, you must show the mathematical equation or definite expression before writing the computed number (e.g. write '\(f(t) = 150 \Rightarrow 400(0.85)^t = 150\)' before stating \(t \approx 6.027\)).
  • 4. Use 3-Decimal Precision: College Board standard is 3 decimal places (truncated or rounded). Store unrounded intermediate values in your calculator variables to prevent intermediate rounding errors.

A cooling liquid has temperature \(T(t) = 20 + 75e^{-0.04t}\) degrees Celsius, where \(t\) is measured in minutes. Write the mathematical setup to find the time when the temperature reaches 45°C, and state the solution to three decimal places.

Step 1 (Setup): Set the model equation equal to 45: \[ 20 + 75e^{-0.04t} = 45 \implies 75e^{-0.04t} = 25 \implies e^{-0.04t} = \frac{1}{3}. \]

Step 2 (Exact analytical solution): Take the natural log of both sides: \[ -0.04t = \ln\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = -\ln(3) \implies t = \frac{\ln(3)}{0.04} = 25\ln(3). \]

Step 3 (3-decimal calculation): \[ t \approx 27.465\text{ minutes}. \]

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

An invasive plant covers an area modeled by \(A(t) = 120(1.15)^t\) square meters, where \(t\) is measured in weeks. Write the equation setup to determine when the area reaches 500 square meters, and find the value of \(t\) to three decimal places with correct units.
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

An invasive plant covers an area modeled by \(A(t) = 120(1.15)^t\) square meters, حيث \(t\) is measured in weeks. Write the equation setup to حدّد عندما the area reaches 500 square meters, and أوجد قيمة \(t\) to three منازل عشرية with correct units.

solution.en:
Setup: Write the equation before numerical solving: \[ 120(1.15)^t = 500 \implies (1.15)^t = \frac{500}{120} = \frac{25}{6}. \]

Solve: Take the natural logarithm: \[ t\ln(1.15) = \ln\left(\frac{25}{6}\right) \implies t = \frac{\ln(25/6)}{\ln(1.15)}. \]

Evaluating on the calculator: \[ t \approx \frac{1.427116}{0.139762} \approx 10.211\text{ weeks}. \] Final answer: 10.211 weeks.
solution.ar:
Setup: Write the equation before numerical solving: \[ 120(1.15)^t = 500 \implies (1.15)^t = \frac{500}{120} = \frac{25}{6}. \]

حل: Take the natural logarithm: \[ t\ln(1.15) = \ln\left(\frac{25}{6}\right) \implies t = \frac{\ln(25/6)}{\ln(1.15)}. \]

Evaluating on the calculator: \[ t \approx \frac{1.427116}{0.139762} \approx 10.211\text{ weeks}. \] Final answer: 10.211 weeks.
